text:
alex: Noticing client sessions that never finish reconnect after a short proxy idle (10s) — clients sit on 'connecting' for minutes :confused:
mei: saw the same. huge reconnect burst then lots of 429s from global limiter when idle timeout fires
santiago: proxy logs show: `session_close idle_timeout=10; set_suppress(true) || rate_limiter:check -> 429` 12 the suppress flag seems to persist when rate-limiter rejects the re-open path
jamie: refresh my memory: suppress prevents immediate session recreation to avoid double billing, right? we added it to stop duplicate-charge windows
alex: correct. it sets a short suppression TTL on close and blocks new session handshakes within that window. the bug is suppression not clearing when a 429 short-circuits the normal reconnect flow
mei: repro I ran locally:
```
# repro: upgrade ws, wait 12s, let proxy cut -> client reconnect flood
for i in {1..60}; do websocket-client open ws://edge.local/connect & done
```
~25% of connections get 429, ~15% hang in connecting state
santiago: snippet from proxy debug:
```
2026-03-22T09:12:01Z proxy.INFO session_close id=xyz idle=10
2026-03-22T09:12:01Z proxy.DEBUG set_suppress key=fp:abc ttl=30000
2026-03-22T09:12:01Z limiter.WARN check client=fp:abc status=429
2026-03-22T09:12:01Z proxy.INFO reject_handshake reason=suppression_active
```
jamie: console shows "reconnecting" forever; we don't surface suppression as a reason so support sees a phantom outage
mei: dashboard counts this as reconnect attempts spike, but billing only records a subset. SLO noise and alert storm
santiago: probable cause: suppression stored in in-memory TTL keyed by fingerprint. rate-limiter path runs early and returns 429 before code that would remove/refresh TTL, leaving suppression extended beyond intended window
alex: fix idea 1: change suppression lifecycle to be idempotent and cleared by the rate-limiter error path (i.e., ensure any terminal path reconciles suppression state). Prefer atomic CAS on suppression key so race can't extend window
jamie: UX idea: expose a non-sensitive expvar "suppression_active" as a client-visible reason so the console can show "suppressed after close" instead of endless reconnect. Add a chart for suppression_count per route
mei: short-term mitigation: lower suppress window from 30s -> 3s behind a feature-flag on edge-canary. reduces user-visible stuck connects while we work on race fix. risk: increases small chance of duplicate billing on double-close
santiago: caution noted. we should quantify duplicate-billing risk before broad rollout
alex: can we run a telemetry query: count of pairs where session_close -> session_open within 2s and both invoked billing service in last 24h? if it's tiny (<0.01%) then 3s canary is acceptable
jamie: I'll add the console mapping + chart (P0). eng-sre should get a temporary alert mute during canary to avoid noisy paging
mei: I've created feature flag entry FF-305: suppress_session_window_ms default=30000 canary=3000 for edge-canary. deploy-bot: starting canary rollout for FF-305 (id=FF-305): 5% -> 25% over 10m
deploy-bot: canary progress: 5% -> 20% -> observing suppression_count, 429_rate, duplicate_billing_estimate
santiago: actions:
- jamie: console chart + reason mapping (P0)
- alex: implement CAS-based suppression lifecycle and handle 429 path cleanup (P0)
- mei: run duplicate-billing telemetry query and post results (P1)
- eng-sre: monitor canary and silence reconnect noise for 20m
jamie: anyone want to pair on console wiring? ping me. I'll also wire up an annotation when FF-305 toggles so support can correlate
alex: i'll pair on the CAS change tomorrow morning
mei: running the billing query now, will update in ~45m :thumbsup:
